title: Comparison and calibration of the 2025 and 2015 American Thyroid Association recurrence-risk classifications in differentiated thyroid cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Comparison and calibration of the 2025 and 2015 American Thyroid Association recurrence-risk classifications in differentiated thyroid cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Objective · abstract-2-1】To determine whether observed rates of structural disease match the risks the 2025 and 2015 ATA classifications assign, and to compare the two systems.

evidence.text: To determine whether observed rates of structural disease match the risks the 2025 and 2015 ATA classifications assign, and to compare the two systems.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Comparison and calibration of the 2025 and 2015 American Thyroid Association recurrence-risk classifications in differentiated thyroid cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patients and methods · abstract-3-1】All 258 consecutive adults with DTC diagnosed in 2017 were classified under both systems using initial postoperative data. The main outcome was structural disease at any assessment, compared against the guideline-assigned ranges.

【Results · abstract-4-1】Sixty-three patients (24.4%) were reclassified, including 52 of 121 (43.0%) low-risk patients upstaged. Thirty-two (12.4%) developed structural disease. Observed 2025 rates were 0.0% (95% CI, 0.0-5.3), 1.5% (0.3-8.0), 15.5% (9.3-24.7), and 47.4% (32.5-62.7) for low, low-intermediate, intermediate-high, and high risk. The low-intermediate interval fell entirely below its assigned 10% to 15% range (P = .013 vs the 10% lower bound); the other categories of both systems were consistent with theirs. No patient upstaged from the 2015 low-risk category developed structural disease. Structural disease later developed in 7 of 14 patients with a biochemically incomplete first response, 2 of 79 indeterminate, and 0 of 129 excellent responses. Discrimination did not differ between the 2 systems (ΔAUC 0.002; 95% CI, -0.031 to 0.036).
